title: MCX Silver Rises 0.56% to ₹251500/kg as Inflation Trade Lifts Precious Metals Complex
summary: The mechanism here is a simultaneous bid in gold and crude — when both rise together, markets are pricing imported inflation, which directly elevates the rupee cost of silver at India's border. With USD/INR at ₹94.52, the transmission is amplified. Import parity arithmetic: COMEX silver near $33.20/oz converts to approximately ₹31,34,240/kg at spot, adjusted by the standard 10% duty-plus-GST factor, theoretical MCX parity lands near ₹248,000–₹250,000/kg, placing current MCX at a modest premium of roughly 0.6–1.5%. Key observation: support is historically watched near ₹249,000; resistance near ₹253,500. Cross-commodity confirmation: MCX Crude is up 0.64%, moving in the same direction, reinforcing the inflationary import-cost narrative rather than challenging it. NatGas down 2.94% is the sole divergence. Watch ₹253,500 and today's US jobless claims data for directional confirmation.
